summary: Configured persistent daily rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1: seven compressed rotations using copytruncate. Live rotation/write continuity and persistence across a verified node reboot both passed.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate, missingok, and notifempty.
Confirmed daily cron invokes logrotate and the global configuration parses the inventory rule.
Performed a live forced rotation while holding app.log open; the existing inode remained writable, prior data was compressed, and the subsequent write reached the active log.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified a changed boot identity, full system recovery, active cron, preserved configuration, active log data, and compressed history.

evidence.requirement: Rotate app.log daily and retain seven rotations
evidence.summary: Daily cron invokes logrotate; the installed rule specifies daily and rotate 7; global parsing reports rotation after one day with seven rotations.
The installed rule enables compression, and the live test produced a valid app.log.1.gz containing the pre-rotation records.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: Across forced rotation, the held file descriptor still targeted app.log and its inode remained unchanged; the post-rotation write appeared in the active log.

Captured healthy baseline boot ef457a88-7774-4b8f-82e6-ccbc965d83e2, native reboot acknowledgement, changed boot 7c622312-1b6b-42f5-bba0-4228f54a6474, and recovered system, cron, rule, active data, and compressed history.
